THE DAANISH UNIVERSITY ISLAMABAD ACT, 2026 
ACT NO. XXII OF 2026 
[18th March, 2026] 
AN 
ACT 
to provide for the establishment of Daanish University, Islamabad 
WHEREAS the Government of Pakistan recognizes the critical importance of emerging 
technologies such as artificial intelligence, quantum computing, advanced materials, renewable energy 
systems, and data science for national development, economic competitiveness,  and the welfare of its 
people; 
AND WHEREAS it is the policy of Government of Pakistan to foster centres of excellence that 
can drive innovation, nurture highly skilled professionals, and generate research o utcomes of global 
significance; 
AND WHEREAS  it is e xpedient to provide for the establishment of Daanish University 
Islamabad and to provide for matters ancillary thereto and connected therewith; 
It is hereby enacted as follows:— 
CHAPTER I 
PRELIMINARY 
1. Short title and commencement. —(1) This Act shall be c alled the Daanish University 
Islamabad Act, 2026. 
(2) It shall come into force at once. 
2. Definitions.—In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context, — 
(i)  “Academic Council” means the Academic Council of the University constituted 
under section 24; 
(ii)  “Authority” means each of the Authorities of the University specified under 
section 19; 
(iii)  “Chancellor” means the Chancellor of the University; 
(iv)  “Commission” means the Higher Education Commission established under the 
Higher Education Commission Ordinance, 2002 (LIII of 2002); 
(v)  “Constituent College ” means an educational institution or Unit, by whatever 
name described, maintained and administered by the University; 
 
Page 5 of 27 
 
(vi)  “Dean” means the head of a faculty or the head of an academic body granted the 
status of a Faculty under this Act or by the Statutes or Regulations; 
(vii)  “Department” means a teaching department maintained and administered, or 
recognized by the University in the manner prescribed; 
(viii)  “Director” means the head of an academic or administrative unit established by 
the University by Statutes or Regulations; 
(ix)  “Emergency Committee” means a committee constituted by the Senate for the 
purposes as mentioned in sub-section (4) of section 12; 
(x)  “Faculty” means an administrative and academic unit of the University consisting 
of one or more departments, as may be prescribed; 
(xi)  “Fund” means the Daanish University Fund established under section 31; 
(xii)  “Government” means the Federal Government of Islamic Republic of Pakistan; 
(xiii)  “prescribed” means prescribed by this Statutes, Regulations or Rules made under 
this Act; 
(xiv)  “Pro-Rector” means the Pro-Rector of the University; 
(xv)  “Registrar” means Registrar of the University; 
(xvi)  “Regulations” means Regulations made under this Act; 
(xvii) “Rector” means Rector of the University; 
(xviii)  “Review Panel” means the Review Panel set up by the Chancellor in accordance 
with the provisions of this Act; 
(xix)  “Rules” means Rules made under this Act; 
(xx)  “Search Committee” means the Search Committee set u p by the Senate under 
this Act; 
(xxi)  “Senate” means the supreme governing body of the University a s constituted 
under section 24; 
(xxii)  “Schedule” means a Schedule to this Act; 
(xxiii)  “Statutes” means Statutes made under this Act; 
(xxiv)  “Teacher” includes Professors Associate Professors, Assistant Professors, and 
Lecturers engaged full-time by the University or by a constituent and such other 
persons as may be declared to be teachers by Regulations; and 
(xxv)  “University” means the Daanish University, Islamabad. 
 
 
Page 6 of 27 
 
CHAPTER II 
THE UNIVERSITY 
3. Establishment and incorporation of the University. —(1) There shall be established  a 
University to be called the Daanish University, Islamabad. 
(2) The University shall consist of the following, namely:- 
(a)  the Chancellor, the members of the Senate, and the Rector; 
(b)  the members of the Authorit of the University established; 
(c)  all Teachers and persons recognized as students of the University in accordance 
with terms prescribed from time to time; and  
(d)  all other University full-time officers and members of the staff of the University 
recognized as such officers and members of the staff of University in accordance 
with terms prescribed from time to time. 
(3) The University shall be a body corporate shall have perpetual succession and a common seal 
and shall have the powers to sue and be sued. 
(4) The University shall be competent to acquire and hold property, both moveable and 
immovable, and to lease, sell or otherwise transfer any movable and immovable property which may 
have become vested in or been acquired by it. 
(5) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the 
University shall have academic, financial and administrative autonomy, including the power to employ 
officers, professors, and other employees on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, subject to 
the provisions of this Act. In particular, and notwithstanding the provisions of any other law, the 
Government or an authority or auditor appointed by the Government shall neither have the power to  
question the allocation of resources approved by  Senate in the annual budget of the University and its 
decision regarding inter alia  investment of any property, grants, bequests, trusts, gifts, contributions 
representing immovable or movable property of the University, nor the policy underlying such allocation 
of resources and decision regarding investment of any property, grants, bequ ests, trusts, gifts, 
contributions representing immovable or movable property of the University. 
(6) The University may provide facilities to the representatives of the Higher Education 
Commission, Pakistan Engineering Council, Pakistan Medical & Dental Co uncil, and other relevant 
organizations for visitation to enable them to verify that the university is maintaining appropriate 
academic standards. 
(7) The University shall be required to strictly comply with the constitutional provisions, 
ideology of Pakistan, law and abide by the social, religious, ethical, and cultural ethos, values, and respect 
cultural and religious sensitivities. 
4. Powers and functions of the University .—The University shall have complete power and 
authority to do all such acts, deeds , matters and things as may be necessary, expedient, ancillary or 
 
Page 7 of 27 
 
desirable to achieve its objectives as a centre of education, learning, research, innovation and 
commercialization, and for the effective administration, governance, development and financin g of the 
University. Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing the University may, — 
(i)  provide for education and scholarship in such branches of knowledge as it may 
deem fit, and to make provision for research, service to society and for the 
application, advancement and dissemination of knowledge in s uch manner as it 
may determine; 
(ii)  prescribe courses of studies to be conducted by it and the con stituent institutions 
or units; 
(iii)  hold examinations and to award and confer degrees, diplom as, certificates and 
other academic distinctions to and on persons who have been admitted to and have 
passed its examinations under prescribed conditions; 
(iv)  prescribe the terms and conditions of employment of the officers, teachers and 
other employees of the University and to lay down terms and conditions that may 
be different from those applicable to government servants in general; 
(v)  engage, where necessary, persons on contracts of specified duration and to specify 
the terms of each engagement; 
(vi)  provide for such instruction for persons not being students of the University as it 
may prescribe, and to grant certificates and diplomas to such persons; 
(vii)  institute programme for the exchange of students and professors between the 
University and other universities, educational institutions and research 
organizations, inside as well as outside Pakistan; 
(viii)  provide career counselling and job search services to students and alumni; 
(ix) maintain linkage with alumni; 
(x)  develop and suggest fund-raising plans; 
(xi)  provide and support the academic development of the Faculty of the University; 
(xii)  confer degrees on persons who have carried on independent resear ch under 
prescribed conditions; 
(xiii)  accept the examinations passe d and the period of study spent by students of the 
University and places of learning equivalent to such examinations and periods of 
study in the University, as it may prescribe, and to withdraw such acceptance; 
(xiv)  co-operate with other Universities, pu blic authorities or private organizations, 
inside as well as outside Pakistan, in such manner and for such purposes as it may 
prescribe; 
 
Page 8 of 27 
 
(xv)  institute Professorships, Associate Professorships, Assistant Professorships and 
Lectureships and any other posts and to appoint persons thereto; 
(xvi)  create posts for research, extension, administration and other related purposes and 
to appoint persons thereto; 
(xvii)  recognize selected members of the teaching staff of university or educational 
universities admitted to the privileges of the university or such other persons as it 
may deem fit, as University Professors, 
(xviii) institute and award financi al assistance to students in need, fellowships, 
scholarships, bursaries, medals and prizes under prescribed conditions; 
(xix)  establish teaching Constituent Colleges, Departments, Faculties, institutes, 
museums and other centers of learning for the develo pment of teaching and 
research, professional and technical training and special studies and to make such 
arrangements for their maintenance, management and admi nistration as it may 
prescribe; 
(xx)  provide for the residence of the students of the Universit y and the Constituent 
Colleges, to institute and maintain halls of residence and to approve or license 
hostels and lodging; 
(xxi)  maintain order, discipline and security on the campuses of the University and the 
Constituent Colleges; 
(xxii)  promote the e xtra-curricular and recreational activities of such students, and to 
make arrangements for promoting their health and general welfare; 
(xxiii)  demand and receive such fees and other charges as it may determine; 
(xxiv)  make provision for research, advisory consultancy or placement services and with 
these objects to enter into arrangements with other Universities, public or private 
bodies, commercial and industrial enterprises under prescribed conditions; 
(xxv)  enter into, carry out, vary or cancel contracts; 
(xxvi)  receive and manage property transferred and grants, contributions made to the 
University and to invest any fund representing such property, grants, bequests, 
trusts, gifts, contributions with the approval of the Senate; and 
(xxvii) provide for the printing and publication of research and other works. 
5. University open to all classes, creeds, etc. —(1) The University shall be open  to all persons 
of any gender religion, race, creed, class, colour or domicile and no person shall be denied privileges of 
the University on these grounds. The University shall uphold the principle of merit in performing all of 
its functions including admission of students, selection and promotion of faculty and staff, and grant of 
specific degree and certificates. 
 
Page 9 of 27 
 
(2) An increase in any fee or charge that is in excess of ten percent per annum on an annualized 
basis from the last such increase may not be made except in special circumstances, and only with the 
approval of the Chancellor. 
(3) The University shall initiate financial aid programmes for students in need, to the extent 
considered feasible by the Senate given the resources available, to enable admission and access to the 
University and the various opportunities, provided by it to be based on merit rather than ability to pay. 
6. Teaching at the University.—(1) All recognized teaching, professional and technical training 
in various courses shall be conducted by the University in the prescribed manner which may include 
lectures, tutorials, discussions, seminars, demonstrations, online and blended learning and other methods 
of instruction as well as practical work in the laboratories, hospitals, workshops and other governmental 
or private organizations. 
(2) The Authority responsible for organ izing recognized teaching shal l be such as may be 
prescribed. 
7. Sub Campuses. —The University may have sub -campuses within Pakistan and abroad with 
the prior approval of Senate relevant Provincial Government and the Commission. 
CHAPTER III 
OFFICERS OF THE UNIVERSITY 
8. Principal Officers. —The University may from time to time appoint such officers as it may 
deem necessary or desirable to achieve its objectives as a center of education, learning, research, 
innovation and commercialization, and for the effecti ve administration, governance, development and 
financing of the University. Without prejudice to generality of the foregoing, the University may have 
the following officers: 
(a)  the Chancellor, 
(b)  the Rector; 
(c)  the Pro Rector; 
(d)  the Deans; 
(e)  the Principals of the Constituent Colleges or units; 
(f)  the Chairpersons of the teaching departments; 
(g)  the Registrar, 
(h)  the Controller of Examinations; 
(i)  the Resident Auditor; and 
(j)  such other persons as may be prescribed by the Statute s or Regulations to be the 
principal officers of the University. 
 
Page 10 of 27 
 
9. Patron. (1) The Prime Minister of Pakistan shall be the Patron of the University. 
(2) The Patron shall preside over the convocation of the University, and in his absence the 
Chancellor shall preside over the convocation. 
 (3) Every proposal to confer an honorary degree shall be subject to confirmation by the Patron. 
(4) In addition to those powers provided for expressly in this A ct, the Patron may in writing 
dolegate any of his powers and functions to the Chancellor. 
10. Visitation.—(1) The Chancellor may, in accordance with the terms and procedures as may 
be prescribed, cause an inspection or inquiry to be made on his own motion in respect of any matter 
connected with the affairs of the Uni versity and shall, from time to time, direct any person or Review 
Panel to inquire into or carry out inspection of— 
(a)  the University, its building, laboratories, libraries, and other facilities. 
(b)  any University, department or hostel maintained by the University; 
(c)  the adequacy of financial and human resources; 
(d)  the teaching, research, curriculum, examination, and othe r matters of the 
University; or 
(e) such other matters as the Chancellor may specify. 
(2) The Chancellor shall c ommunicate, to the Senate, his views with regard to the result of 
visitation and shall, after ascertaining the views, advise the Senate on the action to be taken by it. 
(3) The Senate shall, within such time as may be specified by the Chancellor, communica te to 
him such action, if any, as has been taken or may be proposed to be taken upon the result of visitation.  
11. Chancellor.— The Patron shall appoint the Chairman of Daanish University Trust as the 
University’s Chancellor and Chairperson of the Senate.  
12. Rector.— (1) There shall be a Rector of the University who shall be an eminent academician 
or a distinguished administrator and shall be appointed on such terms and c onditions as may be 
prescribed. 
(2) The Rector shall be the chief officer of the Uni versity responsible for all administrative and 
academic functions of the University, and for ensuring that the provisions of this Act, Statutes, 
Regulations and Rules are faithfully observed to promote the general efficiency and good order of the 
University. The Rector shall have all powers prescribed for this purpose, including administrative control 
over the officers, Professors, and other employees of the University. 
(3) The Rector shall, if present, be entitled to attend any meeting of any Authority or body of the 
University. 
(4) The Rector may, in an emergency that in his opinion requires immediate action ordinarily not 
in the competence of the Rector, take such action and forward, within seventy -two hours, report of the 
 
Page 11 of 27 
 
action taken to the Emergency Committee duly constituted by the Senate for the purposes of dealing with 
emergencies. The Emergency Committee may direct such further action as is considered appropriate. 
(5) Without prejudice to the generality of powers in the foregoing sections, the Rector shall also 
exercise the following powers, namely:— 
(a)  direct professors, officers and other employees of the University to take up such 
assignments in connection with examination, administration and such other 
activities in the University as he may consider necessary for the purposes of the 
University; 
(b)  sanction by re-appropriation an amount not exceeding an amount specified by the 
Senate for an unforeseen item not provided for in the budget and report it to the 
Senate at the next meeting; 
(c)  make appointments of such categories of employees of the University and in such 
manner as may be prescribed by the Statutes; 
(d) suspend, punish and remove, in accordance with prescribed procedure, from 
service officers, professors and other employees of the University except those 
appointed by or with the approval of the Senate; 
(e) delegate, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, any of his powers under 
this Act to an officer or officers of the University; and  
(f)  exercise and perform such other powers and functions as may be prescribed.  
(6) The Rector shall present an annual report before the Senate within three months of the close 
of the academic year. The annual report shall present such information as regards the academic year 
under review as may be prescribed, including disclosure of all relevant facts pertaining to: 
(a)  academics; 
(b)  research; 
(c)  administration; and  
(d)  finances.  
 (7) The Rector’s annual report shall be made available, prior to its presentation before the Senate, 
to all officers and University Professors and shall be published in such numbers as are required to ensure 
its wide circulation.  
 13. Appointment and removal of the Rector and Search Committee.  —(1) The Rector shall 
be appointed by the Senate in the following manner, namely:- 
(a)  a Search Committee for the recommendation of persons suitable for appointment 
as Rector shall be constituted by the Senate on the date and in the manner 
prescribed by the Statutes and shall consist of two eminent members of society 
nominated by the Senate and approved by the Chancellor, of whom one shall be 
 
Page 12 of 27 
 
appointed the convener, one member of the Senate, one University Professor who 
is not member of the Senate, and one academician of eminence not employed by 
the University. The University’s Professor shall be selected by the Senate through 
a process, to be prescribed by Statute, that provides for the recommendation of 
suitable names in general: 
Provided that for the appointment of the first Rector, in lieu of the 
Professor of the University, the Chancellor  shall appoint as a member of the 
Search Committee a professor from any other public or private sector university 
in Pakistan. The Search Committee shall remain in existence till the time of 
appointment of the Rector is made by the Senate; and  
(b) the Sea rch Committee shall recommend a panel of three to the Senate for the 
appointment as Rector: 
Provided that the Senate may decline to appoint any of the three persons 
recommended and seek recommendation of a fresh panel. In the event of a fresh 
recommendation being sought, the Search Committee shall make a proposal to the 
Senate in the prescribed m anner. The Senate shall have the authority to choose 
any one of the three recommended names.  
(2) The Rector shall be appointed for a term of four years on such terms and conditions as may 
be prescribed by the Statutes, and may, upon a resolution of the Se nate supporting such renewal, be re-
appointed once only for a further term of four years. 
(3) The Senate may, pursuant to a resolution in this behalf passed by three -fourths of its 
membership, remove the Rector on the grounds of inefficiency, moral turpitu de, physical or mental 
incapacity, gross misconduct or misuse of position for personal advantage of any kind, 
(4) At any time when the office of the Rector is vacant, or the Rector is absent or is unable to 
perform the functions of his office due to illness or some other cause, the Senate shall ask the senior most 
Pro-Rector to perform the duties of the Rector in his absence. 
14. Pro-Rector.—(1) The Senate may from time to time, on such terms and conditions as it may 
prescribe, appoint on or more Pro -Rectors of the University as it may deem fit . Subject to the overall 
supervision of the Rector, the Pro -Rectors shall assist the Rector on affairs of the University and may 
exercise such powers as may be prescribed by Senate. The Pro Rector may delegate any of his power to 
an appropriate level of management subject to such conditions as he may deemed fit. 
(2) The Pro -Rector shall preside at the convocation o f the University in the absence of the 
Chancellor and Rector. 
15. Directors. —(1) In such manner as may be prescribed, the Senate may from time to time on 
such terms and conditions and having such powers as it may prescribe, appoint such number of Directors 
as it deems appropriate, including, inter alia, Director Finance, Director Human Resources.  
(2) A Director shall hold office for a term of four years and may, upon a resolution of the Senate 
supporting such renewal, be re-appointed once only for a further term of four years. 
 
Page 13 of 27 
 
(3) A Director shall hold office until the expiry of his term, or earlier resignation, or removal by 
the Senate on grounds of misconduct or as may otherwise be prescribed. 
(4) The job descriptions, terms and conditions of service, and criteria for performance evaluation 
of the Directors shall be such as may be determined by the Senate. 
16. Registrar.—(1) There shall be a Registrar of the University to be appointed by the Senate on 
the recommendation of the Selection Board, on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed. 
(2) The experience as well as the professional and academic qual ification necessary for 
appointment to the post of Registrar shall be as may be prescribed. 
(3) The Registrar shall be be a full-time officer of the University and shall,— 
(a)  be the administrative head of the secretariat of the University and be responsi ble 
for the provision of secretariat support to the Authorities of the University; 
(b)  be the custodian of the common seal and the academic records of the University; 
(c)  maintain a register of registered graduates in the prescribed manner; 
(d)  supervise the process of election, appointment, or nomination of members to the 
various authorities and other bodies in the prescribed manner; and 
(e)  perform such other duties as may be prescribed. 
(4) The term of office of the Registrar shall be four years, and may be renewed once for a further 
term of four years: 
Provided that the Senate may, on the advice of the Rector, terminate the appointment of the  
Registrar on grounds of inefficiency or misconduct in the prescribed manner. 
17. Controller of Examin ation.—(1) There shall  be a Controller of Examination of the 
University, to be appointed by the Senate on the recommendation of the Selection Board, on such terms 
and conditions as may be prescribed. 
(2) The minimum qualification necessary for appointment to the post of the Controller of 
Examination shall be as may be prescribed. 
(3) The Controller of Examination shall be a full -time officer of the University and shall be 
responsible for all the matters connected with the conduct of examination and perform such other duties 
as may be prescribed. 
 (4) The Controller of Examination shall be appointed for a renewable term of four years: 
Provided that the Senate may, on the advice of the Rector, terminate the appointment of the 
Controller of Examination on the grounds of inefficiency or misconduct in the prescribed manner. 
18. Resident Auditor.— (1) There shall be a Resident Auditor of the University, to be appointed 
by the Senate on the recommendation of the Selection Board, on such terms and c onditions as may be 
prescribed. 
 
Page 14 of 27 
 
(2) The Resident Auditor shall be a full -time officer of the University and shall be responsible 
for pre-audit of all payments from the Fund. He shall perform any other duty assigned by the Senat e, 
Academic Council and Rector. 
(3) The minimum experience as well as the professional and academic qualifications necessary 
for the appointment to the post of Resident Auditor shall be as may be prescribed.  
(4) The Senate may, on the advice of Rector, terminate the services of the Resident Auditor 
appointed on regular basis on grounds of inefficiency or misconduct, in the prescribed procedure. 
CHAPTER IV 
AUTHORITIES OF THE UNIVERSITY 
19. Authorities.— (1) The following shall be the Authorities of the University, namely: — 
(a)  Authorities established by this Act: — 
(i)  the Senate; 
(ii)  Executive Committee; and 
(iii)  the Academic Council. 
(b)  Authorities that may be established by the Statutes: — 
(i)  Board of Advanced Studies and Research; 
(ii)  Board of Studies; 
(iii)  Selection Board; 
(iv)  Finance and Planning Committee; 
(v)  Search Committee for the appointment of the Rector; 
(vi)  Quality Enhancement Committee; and 
(vii)  Discipline Committee. 
(2) The Senate and the Academic Council may set up such other committees or sub-committees, 
by whatever name described, as are considered desirable through Statutes or Regulations. Such 
committees or subcommittees shall be Authorities of the University for the purposes of this Act. 
20. Senate. —(1) The general supervision and control of the affairs, and power to lay down 
polices of the University shall vest in the Senate. The members of the Board of Trustees of Daanish 
University Trust, a Not -For-Profit Trust registered under the Punjab Trust Act , 2020 shall be the 
members of the Senate of the University. The Chancellor of the University shall also serve as  the 
chairperson of the Senate. 
(2) The nominated members of the Senate shall hold office for a period of four years and  shall 
be eligible for re-nomination on the expiry of his term unless earlier terminated under the law. 
 
Page 15 of 27 
 
(3) The office of a nominated member of the Senate shall become vacant if he ceases to be a 
member of the board of trustees of the Daanish University Trust or resigns or fails  to attend three 
consecutive meetings of the Senate without sufficient cause or leave of absence. 
(4) A casual vacancy in the office of a member of the Senate shall be filled by a person nominated 
by the nominating authority which had nominated the member whose vacancy is to be filled. 
(5) The quorum for a meeting of the Senate shall be two-thirds of the total number of its members. 
Every member shall have one vote. In the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have and may exe rcise a 
second or casting vote. 
(6) The Senate shall meet at least twice in a calendar year. 
(7) No act or proceedings of the Senate shall be invalid by reason only of the existence of a 
vacancy in or any defect in the constitution of the Senate. 
(8) Service on the Senate shall be on an ho norary basis, however, actual expenses m ay be 
reimbursed as prescribed. 
21. Powers and functions of the Senate. — (1) The Senate shall have the power of supervision 
over the University and shall hold the Rector and the Authorities accountable for all the functions of the 
University. The Senate shall have all powers in relation to the University not expressly vested in an 
Authority or officer by this Act and all other powers not expressly mentioned by this Act that are 
necessary for the performance of its functions. 
(2) The Senate shall be the executive body of the University and shall, subject to the provisions 
of this Act and the Statutes, exercise general supervision over the affairs an d management of the 
University. 
(3) Without prejudice to the generality  of the foregoing powers, the Senate shall have the 
following powers, namely:- 
(a)  to approve the proposed annual plan of work, the annual and revised budgets, the 
annual report and the annual statement of account; 
(b)  to hold, control and lay down policy for the administration of the property, funds 
and investments of the University, including the approval of the sale and purchase 
or acquisition of immovable property; 
(c)  to oversee the quality and relevance of the University's academic programmes and 
to review the academic affairs and ensure its alignment with vision and mission 
of Danish University; 
(d)  to approve establishment of Facultics and appointment of the Deans, Professors, 
Associate professors and such other senior faculty and senior admin istrators as 
may be prescribed; 
(e)  to University schemes, directions and guidelines for the terms and conditions of 
Appointment of all officers, professors and other employees of the University;

CHAPTER VII

33. University Procurement.—(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Public

made thereunder, the University shall have the power to frame, adopt and administer its p rocurement 
policies, procedures and guidelines for the acquisition of goods, works and services.

rules and regulations made thereunder shall not apply to any procurement made by the University under 
this Act.

teacher of other employee of the University shall be removed from office, reduced in rank, or 
compulsorily retired from office unless he is given a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against 
the action proposed to be taken.

Rector, Teacher or other employee of the University or  altering or interpreting to his disadvantage the 
prescribed terms or conditions of his service, he shall, where the order is passed by any officer or 
professor of the University other than the Rector, have the right to appeal to Rector against the order, 
and where the order is passed by the Rector, have the right to appeal to the Senate against the order.

attainment of such age or tenute of service as may be prescribed.

professors and other employees' schemes, as may be prescribed, for the provision of post -employment 
benefits as well as health and life insurance while in service.

newly constituted Authority is elected, appointed, or nominated, his term of office as fixed under this 
Act, shall commence from such date as may be prescribed. 
(2) Where a member who has accepted any other assignment or for any other similar  reason 
remains absent from the University for a period of not less than six months he shall be deemed to have  
resigned and vacated his seat. 
39. Filling of casual vacancies in Authorities. —Any casual vacancy in any Authority shall be 
filled, as soon as co nveniently may be, in the same manner and by the same person or authority which 
had appointed him and the person appointed to the vacancy shall be a member of such Authority for the 
residue of the term for which the person whose place he fills would have been a member. 
40. Flaws in the constitution of Authority. —Where there is a flaw in the constitution of an 
Authority, as constituted by this Act, the Statutes or the Regulations on account of the abolition of a 
specified office or because an organization, u niversities or other body outside the University has been 
dissolved or has ceased to function, or because of some other similar reason, such flaw shall be removed 
in such manner as the Senate may direct. 
41. Proceedings of Authorities not invalidated by vacancies. —No act, resolution or decision 
of any Authority shall be invalid by reason of any vacancy in the Authority doing, passing, or making it 
or by reason of any want of qualification or invalidity in the election, appointment or nomination of any 
de facto member of the Authority, whether present or absent. 
42. Removal of difficulty. —(1) If any question ari ses as to the interpretation of any of the 
provisions of this Act, it shall be placed before the Senate whose decision thereon shall be final.

make such order, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, as may appear to him to be necessary 
for removing the difficulty.

provision has been made as respects the authority by whom, or the time at which, or the manner in which, 
it shall be done, then it shall be done by such authority, at such time, or in such manner as the Senate 
may direct after obtaining the views of, the Commission.
